findings.summary: The pinned help string ``break the summary down by `task` or `session` `` does not render as intended. pflag's UnquoteUsage removes only the first pair of backquotes and uses that word as the placeholder. `vloop metrics --help` would print `--by task   break the summary down by task or `session``, with literal backticks and a placeholder that still says `task`. The regenerated docs/guide/commands.md would show the same.
findings.evidence: ~/go/pkg/mod/github.com/spf13/pflag@v1.0.9/flag.go:592-606 (UnquoteUsage returns after the first backquoted pair); go.mod pins pflag v1.0.9; docs/guide/commands.md:285 shows the current rendering `- `--by task`: break the summary down by task`
findings.fix: Pin a usage string with exactly one backquoted word, for example ``break the summary down by `view`: task or session``, so the help reads `--by view   break the summary down by view: task or session`. Use that exact wording in P1 Docs.

findings.section: Executive summary (goal) / P4 README and header comments
findings.summary: The brief says the kit needs only go, copilot and gh (plus claude), and P4 has the README and every script's header say so. But bypass.sh also needs perl: it takes every timestamp from `perl -MTime::HiRes`. A README that follows P4 would leave a real dependency out.
findings.evidence: tools/copilot-acceptance/bypass.sh:17 `now='perl -MTime::HiRes=time -e "printf q(%.3f), time"'`, used at lines 27 and 30
findings.fix: In P4 (and the goal line), say that bypass.sh also needs perl, and have its header comment name it. Or replace the perl timestamp, which leaves what the probe tests unchanged; that route needs a line in the contract.

findings.section: Behaviour contract / P3; Decided here (fixture paths)
findings.summary: hook.py reads VLOOP_HOOK_PHASE (default `review`) and writes it into the hooks file as `--phase <phase>`. The README documents it as the way to probe a second-review session. P3 never names it, and the tests unset it in both runs. A Go port that hard-codes `review` would match every golden and pass every gate, while the second-review hook probe would silently use the wrong phase.
findings.evidence: tools/copilot-acceptance/hook.py:59 `phase = os.environ.get("VLOOP_HOOK_PHASE", "review")`; tools/copilot-acceptance/README.md:70-73; the brief says 'VLOOP_HOOK_PHASE is unset in both runs' and has no worked-example line that sets it
findings.fix: In P3, say that `hook forms` and `hook failure` read VLOOP_HOOK_PHASE as hook.py does (default review). Add a worked-example line: `hook forms` with VLOOP_HOOK_PHASE=second-review → hooks/vloop-fence.json's bash and powershell hold `--phase second-review`. That can be a golden generated with the variable set, or a Go-only assertion.

findings.summary: The clone is named `url-shortener-tests/b34-backstop`, a path that does not resolve from this repository or from any stated root. It exists at ~/source/personal/url-shortener-tests/b34-backstop, and B32's brief writes it in that form.
findings.evidence: docs/briefs/B20261102-2101-b32-i84-gates-through-the-named-surface.loop-brief.md:328 uses `~/source/personal/url-shortener-tests/b32-terra61`; ~/source/personal/url-shortener-tests/b34-backstop holds 16 copilot sessions with credits and cost_source estimated

decisions: The per-session view is `vloop metrics --by session`, not a new `vloop sessions` command. Agree.

`by_session` joins metrics/v4 as an optional property instead of a v5. It is emitted in every --json document, and so in the close snapshot .vloop/state/metrics/<run id>.json, with each denial's text (whole commands), and in --workspace --json. `export` drops it. The snapshot growth is not stated explicitly; worth knowing.
Each denial's `text` is the first non-empty of message, command, file_path, tool_input.command and tool_input.file_path. This covers every denial shape in this repository's records.
The kit becomes one Go program, run with `go run ./tools/copilot-acceptance/kit`, in this module and not a vloop subcommand; jq is rejected. Agree.

The Go port is byte-for-byte except the session tables, gated on goldens the base's Python prints, regenerated by gen.sh in task 2's gate from `git show <base>:`. Task 2's and the close task's gates therefore need python3 on the gate machine; no go test does.

The six reports' own session tables are dropped for `vloop metrics --by session` blocks. The reports lose their per-report columns (gate-review's round, the second report's filter to session/v4 records), and the text no longer shows which schema version each record was written as (only INVALID records name it; the JSON keeps `schema`).

Schema checks validate each record against its own `schema` field rather than the fixed session/v3 or session/v4 the Python checked. A record written with the wrong version now passes if it is valid for the version it claims.

Small choices: `#` is three digits; credits prints `-` when absent and `0.00` when 0; a second-review row has phase second-review; the `second` fixture has one run folder; the goldens live in kit/testdata/ with @DIR@ substitution.
Scripts call `go -C "$top" run …` and make their directory argument absolute (pwd -P); hook.sh and bypass.sh gain `top`. This fixes today's latent bug with relative directory arguments.
